question: What should we treat as activation for new users, and how confident are you?

must_mention.why: names the first agent action as activation
flags that the result is observational

must_not_claim.why: does not crown question-asking as activation

reference_good: Treat the first completed agent action as activation. External users who complete one in week 0 retain at {act_agent} at week 8 (n=9,568), versus {act_question} for question-only users. Confidence is medium: this is observational, so confirm with an onboarding experiment that nudges a first agent action.
reference_bad: Activation should be the first question. Most users ask one, so it is easy to hit and retention looks great.

question: What is our week-8 retention?
reference_good: For external users, week-8 retention is {ret_external}. Including the internal customer-zero deployment raises it to {ret_all}, but internal use is mandated, so report external users separately.
reference_bad: Week-8 retention is 33% across all users, which is strong.

question: Should we push the desktop app because it drives retention?

must_mention.why: explains the lift disappears within segments

must_not_claim.why: does not claim desktop causes retention

reference_good: No. Desktop users retain {desktop_agg} better in aggregate, but within each segment the difference is about zero. It is confounded by mix: the internal rollout installed it by default.
reference_bad: Yes. The desktop app drives retention by 20 points, so we should push it to everyone.

question: Which prospect accounts should business development contact this week, and which signups should they ignore?

must_mention.why: recommends testing outreach with a holdout

reference_good: Start with the top-scored accounts: each has a dozen or more independent users across several functions, most completed an agent action in their first week, and several shared agents. Ignore the accounts flagged as noise: their signups came in one week from a webinar spike with low activation. Keep a holdout of qualified accounts so outreach can prove its lift.
reference_bad: Contact every company with more than 15 signups, starting with the biggest.

question: How many independent freemium users does a company need before we start an enterprise sales motion?

must_mention.why: notes the rule is learned from limited outcomes or must be refit

must_not_claim.why: does not recommend a raw sign-up count

reference_good: Start the motion once a company has {trigger_k} or more activated independent users; those companies convert at several times the baseline rate, and one user short of that, run champion enablement instead. Count activated users, not sign-ups, because webinar spikes inflate sign-ups. Several rules are statistically tied on the contracts we have, so refit the rule each quarter.
reference_bad: Once a company reaches 10 sign-ups, hand it to sales.

question: Can we use the Slack, Teams or Jira workspaces people connect to figure out where they work?

must_mention.why: names the side-project or community false positive

must_not_claim.why: does not treat any matching workspace name as proof

reference_good: Yes, with guards. Trust a workspace's verified domain; treat a matching name as a clue that needs a colleague resolved by work email to corroborate it; drop guest memberships, since contractors sit in client workspaces; and drop community or side-project workspaces, like a school robotics Slack whose members already resolve to several companies. Naive matching made many wrong attributions and invented phantom sales-ready accounts.
reference_bad: Yes. Map every workspace named after a company to that company and count its members as adopters.

question: Should we give users credits for sharing to drive viral growth?

must_mention.why: pays on the recipient's activation, not the share or sign-up
ties rewards to account stage (same company before a contract, external after)
does not pay for licensed colleagues

must_not_claim.why: does not recommend paying per share sent

reference_good: Yes, but pay when the recipient completes their first agent action, not when a share is sent or a sign-up happens. Before a company has a contract, reward shares to colleagues in the same company; after a contract, reward shares to customers and partners outside it, and never pay for colleagues who are already licensed. In simulation this keeps the pipeline gains at about a tenth of the rewards.
reference_bad: Yes. Reward every share with credits; more shares means more growth.
